hook.text: Two billion people suffer micronutrient deficiencies — biofortification breeds vitamins and minerals into staple crops.

buildup.text: HarvestPlus developed iron-rich pearl millet and zinc-rich rice — conventional breeding guided by nutritional targets.

discovery.text: Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes provide beta-carotene — adopted by 10 million households in sub-Saharan Africa.

twist.text: Biofortification works only if farmers adopt and consumers accept the new varieties — taste and yield must match.

climax.text: CRISPR now accelerates biofortification — editing existing varieties to accumulate more micronutrients directly.

punchline.text: Breed the nutrition in — biofortification feeds and nourishes at once.

quiz.question: What is biofortification?
options: Adding vitamin supplements to processed food products
Breeding or engineering staple crops to contain higher levels of essential micronutrients
Spraying crops with mineral solutions to increase their nutrient content

details.summary: Biofortification enhances the nutritional content of crops through breeding or genetic engineering. By increasing vitamins, minerals, or essential amino acids in staple foods, biofortification addresses hidden hunger in populations that rely on limited diets.
details.whyItMatters: Over two billion people suffer from micronutrient deficiencies. Biofortified crops deliver nutrients through foods people already eat, providing a sustainable and cost-effective alternative to supplements or dietary diversification.
takeaways: Biofortification increases vitamins and minerals in staple food crops
Iron-enriched beans and zinc-enriched wheat are already deployed globally
It addresses hidden hunger without requiring dietary behavior changes

faq.question: What is the difference between fortification and biofortification?
faq.answer: Fortification adds nutrients during food processing, like adding iodine to salt. Biofortification breeds or engineers the nutrients directly into the crop itself, so the nutrition is inherent in the harvested grain without any processing step.

faq.question: How successful has biofortification been so far?
faq.answer: HarvestPlus has released over 300 biofortified crop varieties in 60 countries, reaching millions of farming households. Studies show improved iron and zinc status in populations consuming biofortified beans, pearl millet, and wheat.
